einzeiler: Ray Hadley testifies in Alan Jones trial, revealing bitter radio rivalries.
kurzfassung: Radio broadcaster Ray Hadley took the witness stand in week five of Alan Jones's indecent assault trial. Testifying for the prosecution, Hadley detailed a decades-long rivalry and explosive text messages exchanged between the former colleagues. The defense argued that Hadley's animosity and a secret contract fueled the allegations against Jones.
stichpunkte: Ray Hadley testified as a key prosecution witness regarding disclosures made by a former 2GB employee.
The defense cross-examined Hadley about his bitter rivalry and past text messages insulting Jones.
Court revelations exposed a secret 2018 contract that would have doubled Hadley's salary to take over the breakfast slot.
Judge Glenn Walsh expressed frustration with endless tangents into internal station politics.
Hadley recounted helping the complainant speak anonymously to a journalist in 2019.
The trial is expected to continue through December, with a judgment anticipated around February.

clips.text: The defense accused the witness of winking at the prosecution, though he later insisted he was aiming at someone else in the room.

clips.hook: Judge warns against chasing every rabbit down every hole
clips.text: The presiding judge voiced annoyance at protracted questioning about station politics, warning that such tangents would unnecessarily prolong the proceedings.
Confronted with a text message expressing affection to a sick colleague, the witness offered a peculiar clarification about cemetery plots.

clips.hook: Doubling a salary without changing shifts
clips.text: The witness explained that he was quite content to stay in his morning time slot because rival negotiations had inadvertently doubled his pay anyway.

beschreibung: As talkback titan Ray Hadley took the witness box in Alan Jones’s indecent assault and sexual touching trial, the court heard accounts of a tearful disclosure, a secret contract and decades of professional animosity. Under cross-examination, explosive text messages laid bare the full extent of the station’s high-stakes internal power struggle. Host Nour Haydar and Guardian media correspondent Amanda Meade are back to take you through week five of the trial of Alan Jones
